families.migration: hybrid (classical Ed25519 + ML-DSA dual signatures during transition)
families.name: Ed25519
families.quantum_threat: Shor's algorithm: a cryptographically relevant quantum computer breaks Ed25519 signatures, so any signature recorded on the ledger is forgeable after the fact and any long-lived validator key is compromisable.
references: FIPS 204 (ML-DSA), Module-Lattice-Based Digital Signature Standard, NIST, final 13 August 2024, effective 14 August 2024 — candidate replacement signature scheme
FIPS 205 (SLH-DSA), Stateless Hash-Based Digital Signature Standard, NIST, final 13 August 2024, effective 14 August 2024 — conservative replacement signature scheme
families.role: account signatures, validator manifest signing, validation signatures

families.migration: hybrid (classical secp256k1 + ML-DSA dual signatures during transition)
families.name: secp256k1 (ECDSA)
families.quantum_threat: Shor's algorithm: breaks secp256k1 ECDSA the same way it breaks Ed25519. Default account key type (WalletPropose.cpp) and the validator key type (ValidationCreate.cpp) are both secp256k1.
references: FIPS 204 (ML-DSA), Module-Lattice-Based Digital Signature Standard, NIST, final 13 August 2024, effective 14 August 2024 — candidate replacement signature scheme
families.role: account signatures (default key type), validator key generation, peer-handshake session signatures

families.name: SHA-512-Half (sha512Half)
families.quantum_threat: Grover's algorithm only: a 256-bit sha512Half output retains about 128 bits of post-quantum preimage/collision resistance. No Shor exposure. No change required on quantum grounds alone; hash agility is absent, so a future hash replacement would be a coordinated change.
references: FIPS 180-4, Secure Hash Standard (SHA-512), NIST — hash function underlying sha512Half
families.role: ledger hashes, transaction IDs, ledger entry indexes, server-definitions hash

families.absence_evidence: src/rpc_inventory.py case-insensitive grep for ML-KEM/ML-DSA/SLH-DSA/Kyber/Dilithium/SPHINCS over src/ + include/: 0 file hits
families.migration: hybrid (ML-KEM hybrid with existing key exchange, when a PQ transport is adopted)
families.name: ML-KEM
families.quantum_threat: Absence, not exposure: no key-exchange primitive in the tree can be replaced by ML-KEM without new code. TLS key exchange is delegated to OpenSSL and is classical-only under the default configuration.
references: FIPS 203 (ML-KEM), Module-Lattice-Based Key-Encapsulation Mechanism Standard, NIST, final 13 August 2024, effective 14 August 2024 (Federal Register Vol. 89 No. 157)
families.role: post-quantum key encapsulation (key exchange) — no in-tree role yet

families.name: ML-DSA
families.quantum_threat: Absence, not exposure: no signature path in the tree can emit or verify ML-DSA without new code. Every signing method in the inventory verifies Ed25519/secp256k1 only.
references: FIPS 204 (ML-DSA), Module-Lattice-Based Digital Signature Standard, NIST, final 13 August 2024, effective 14 August 2024 (Federal Register Vol. 89 No. 157)
families.role: post-quantum digital signatures — no in-tree role yet

families.absence_evidence: src/rpc_inventory.py case-insensitive grep for ML-KEM/ML-DSA/SLH-DSA/Kyber/Dilithium/SPHINCS over src/ + include/: 0 file hits
families.migration: hybrid (candidate for infrequent signatures only, e.g. validator manifests)
families.name: SLH-DSA
families.quantum_threat: Absence, not exposure: no signature path in the tree can emit or verify SLH-DSA without new code. Its large signatures (about 7.9 KB to 49 KB per FIPS 205) make it a poor fit for per-transaction use; a candidate only for infrequent signatures such as validator manifests.
references: FIPS 205 (SLH-DSA), Stateless Hash-Based Digital Signature Standard, NIST, final 13 August 2024, effective 14 August 2024 (Federal Register Vol. 89 No. 157)
families.role: post-quantum hash-based digital signatures — no in-tree role yet

families.migration: hybrid (ML-KEM hybrid TLS key exchange via OpenSSL configuration, when available)
families.name: TLS 1.2 transport (OpenSSL)
families.quantum_threat: Shor's algorithm against the classical key exchange (ECDH/RSA) negotiated by OpenSSL under the default cipher list; a recorded session could be decrypted retrospectively. No PQ or hybrid key exchange is configured in-tree.
references: FIPS 203 (ML-KEM), Module-Lattice-Based Key-Encapsulation Mechanism Standard, NIST, final 13 August 2024 — candidate hybrid KEM for TLS key exchange
families.role: encryption and peer authentication for RPC (HTTP/WebSocket) and peer connections; key exchange delegated to OpenSSL
